From: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jan 2022 08:43:28 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] af_unix: annote lockless accesses to unix_tot_inflight &
 gc_in_progress

wait_for_unix_gc() reads unix_tot_inflight & gc_in_progress
without synchronization.

Adds READ_ONCE()/WRITE_ONCE() and their associated comments
to better document the intent.

diff --git a/net/unix/scm.c b/net/unix/scm.c
index 052ae709ce28..aa27a02478dc 100644
--- a/net/unix/scm.c
+++ b/net/unix/scm.c
@@ -60,7 +60,8 @@ void unix_inflight(struct user_struct *user, struct file *fp)
 		} else {
 			BUG_ON(list_empty(&u->link));
 		}
-		unix_tot_inflight++;
+		/* Paired with READ_ONCE() in wait_for_unix_gc() */
+		WRITE_ONCE(unix_tot_inflight, unix_tot_inflight + 1);
 	}
 	user->unix_inflight++;
 	spin_unlock(&unix_gc_lock);
@@ -80,7 +81,8 @@ void unix_notinflight(struct user_struct *user, struct file *fp)
 
 		if (atomic_long_dec_and_test(&u->inflight))
 			list_del_init(&u->link);
-		unix_tot_inflight--;
+		/* Paired with READ_ONCE() in wait_for_unix_gc() */
+		WRITE_ONCE(unix_tot_inflight, unix_tot_inflight - 1);
 	}
 	user->unix_inflight--;
 	spin_unlock(&unix_gc_lock);
-- 
2.25.1



diff --git a/net/unix/garbage.c b/net/unix/garbage.c
index 12e2ddaf887f..d45d5366115a 100644
--- a/net/unix/garbage.c
+++ b/net/unix/garbage.c
@@ -192,8 +192,11 @@ void wait_for_unix_gc(void)
 {
 	/* If number of inflight sockets is insane,
 	 * force a garbage collect right now.
+	 * Paired with the WRITE_ONCE() in unix_inflight(),
+	 * unix_notinflight() and gc_in_progress().
 	 */
-	if (unix_tot_inflight > UNIX_INFLIGHT_TRIGGER_GC && !gc_in_progress)
+	if (READ_ONCE(unix_tot_inflight) > UNIX_INFLIGHT_TRIGGER_GC &&
+	    !READ_ONCE(gc_in_progress))
 		unix_gc();
 	wait_event(unix_gc_wait, gc_in_progress == false);
 }
@@ -213,7 +216,9 @@ void unix_gc(void)
 	if (gc_in_progress)
 		goto out;
 
-	gc_in_progress = true;
+	/* Paired with READ_ONCE() in wait_for_unix_gc(). */
+	WRITE_ONCE(gc_in_progress, true);
+
 	/* First, select candidates for garbage collection.  Only
 	 * in-flight sockets are considered, and from those only ones
 	 * which don't have any external reference.
@@ -299,7 +304,10 @@ void unix_gc(void)
 
 	/* All candidates should have been detached by now. */
 	BUG_ON(!list_empty(&gc_candidates));
-	gc_in_progress = false;
+
+	/* Paired with READ_ONCE() in wait_for_unix_gc(). */
+	WRITE_ONCE(gc_in_progress, false);
+
 	wake_up(&unix_gc_wait);
 
  out:

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/unix/scm.c`**
   - The `unix_inflight` function was modified to replace the direct increment of `unix_tot_inflight` with a `WRITE_ONCE()` call, which ensures that the increment operation is performed atomically and without data races. A comment was added to indicate that this is paired with a `READ_ONCE()` in the `wait_for_unix_gc()` function.
   - Similarly, in the `unix_notinflight` function, the direct decrement of `unix_tot_inflight` was replaced with a `WRITE_ONCE()` call, along with a comment indicating its pairing with `READ_ONCE()` in `wait_for_unix_gc()`.

2. **File: `net/unix/garbage.c`**
   - In the `wait_for_unix_gc()` function, the check for `unix_tot_inflight` and `gc_in_progress` was updated to use `READ_ONCE()` for both variables, ensuring that the reads are also atomic and synchronized.
   - The `gc_in_progress` variable is now set to `true` using `WRITE_ONCE()` when garbage collection starts, with a comment indicating its pairing with `READ_ONCE()` in `wait_for_unix_gc()`.
   - At the end of the `unix_gc()` function, `gc_in_progress` is set to `false` using `WRITE_ONCE()`, again with a comment indicating its pairing with `READ_ONCE()` in `wait_for_unix_gc()`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications establish a synchronization mechanism between the `unix_inflight`, `unix_notinflight`, and `wait_for_unix_gc` functions. By using `READ_ONCE()` and `WRITE_ONCE()`, the patch addresses a data race condition reported by the Kernel Concurrency Sanitizer. The comments added in the code clarify the relationships between the read and write operations, ensuring that the increments and decrements of `unix_tot_inflight` and the state of `gc_in_progress` are safely accessed across different contexts, preventing potential inconsistencies and race conditions.
